newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS TO SELL RADISSON SAS HOTELS - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: SAS TO SELL RADISSON SAS HOTELS - REPORT.

text.p: Scandinavian airline SAS will shortly sell its Radisson SAS hotel operations, or get new part owners and financiers, Swedish daily Dagens Industri said on Thursday.
The hotel chain consists of 91 hotels of which SAS owns five hotels.
Sources told the newspaper two bidding rounds have passed with three buyers remaining at around 2.3 billion crowns.

The hottest candidate to buy the group is the British company Millennium & Copthorne Hotels, owned by CDL Hotels International, which in turn is controlled by Singapore billionaire Kwek Leng Beng, the newspaper said.
"Of course buying candidates turn up at an evaluation process but we haven't taken any decision to sell the hotel operations yet," SAS spokesman Peter Forssman was quoted as saying.
SAS's hotel operations posted a profit of 65 million crowns last year, up from 34 million crowns in 1995. Radisson SAS is Europe's fastest growing hotel chain, the newspaper said.
